messages.content:
**Summary of Source Gathering for Week 7 (Days 43-49)**

**What I Did:**
Performed targeted web searches for each focus area:
1. Infant growth and feeding schedules (7-week-old baby)
2. Maternal physical recovery (pelvic floor and diastasis recti at 7 weeks postpartum)
3. Introducing solids preparation (readiness signs, typical timeline)

**What I Found:**

*Infant Growth & Feeding Schedules:*
- **Motherly**: "7-Week-Old Baby Feeding Schedule & Amounts" – guidance on feeding frequency, amounts, and milk supply tips. (https://www.mother.ly/parenting/two-month-old-baby-feeding-guides-schedules/7-week-old-baby-feeding-schedule-and-amounts/)
- **Fairhaven Health**: "How Much Should I Be Feeding My 7 Week Old?" – recommends 3-4 ounces every 2-3 hours, with adjustments for growth spurts. (https://www.fairhavenhealth.com/blogs/fairhaven-health-library/how-much-should-i-be-feeding-my-7-week-old)
- **CDC**: "How Much and How Often to Breastfeed" – notes 8-12 feedings per 24 hours and vitamin D supplementation guidance. (https://www.cdc.gov/infant-toddler-nutrition/breastfeeding/how-much-and-how-often.html)
- **Parents.com**: Feeding chart indicating 7-8 ounces per feeding by this age, with emphasis on hunger/fullness cues. (https://www.parents.com/baby/feeding/baby-feeding-chart-how-much-and-when-to-feed-infants-the-first-year/)

*Maternal Physical Recovery:*
- **Pelvic Floor:**
  - The Pelvic Studio: Postpartum recovery guide highlighting constipation avoidance for pelvic floor health. (https://www.thepelvicstudio.com/blog/6weekpostpartumrecovery)
  - The Vagina Whisperer: First 8 weeks postpartum exercises – walking, gentle core work, pelvic floor strengthening; avoidance of high-impact activities. (https://thevagwhisperer.com/2022/01/18/first-8-weeks-postpartum-exercises/)
  - My Health Alberta: Pelvic floor exercise progression (start 3-second holds, increase weekly). (https://myhealth.alberta.ca/Health/aftercareinformation/pages/conditions.aspx?hwid=acn5187)
  - NIH/PMC: Maximizing recovery timeline – pelvic floor recovery thought to be maximized by 4-6 months postnatal. (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9528725/)
- **Diastasis Recti:**
  - Cleveland Clinic: Overview of causes, treatment, and natural healing timeline. (https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/22346-diastasis-recti)
  - University of Utah Health: Signs of diastasis recti (doming/coning) and typical 6-week check assessment. (https://healthcare.utah.edu/womens-health/postpartum/pelvic-floor-complications/diastasis-recti)
  - NIH/PMC Scoping Review: Notes natural resolution often occurs in first 8 weeks postpartum, with possible ongoing recovery up to 6 months. (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11023973/)

*Introducing Solids Preparation:*
- **Solid Starts**: Readiness signs – most babies ready around 6 months; emphasizes looking for developmental cues rather than age alone. (https://solidstarts.com/readiness/)
- **PatPat**: Complete first foods guide (4-6 months) – lists readiness signs: head control, sitting with support, loss of tongue thrust reflex. (https://www.patpat.com/blogs/baby-food/starting-solids-first-foods-guide-4-6-months)
- **Happy Family Organics**: Signs of readiness – head control, ability to sit up, interest in food. (https://www.happyfamilyorganics.com/learning-center/article/introducing-solids-signs-of-readiness/)
- **Kidecology**: Gross/oral motor signs – ability to sit upright and disappearance of tongue-thrust reflex. (https://www.kidecology.com/baby-ready-for-solids.html)
- **Ready Set Grow Nutrition**: Advises not to start solids before 4 months (17 weeks) due to immature immune/digestive systems. (https://www.readysetgrownutrition.com/blog/signs-of-readiness-for-solids)

**Files Created or Modified:**
No files were created or modified during this session; all information was gathered via web search and retained in the conversation context.

**Issues Encountered:**
None – all searches returned successful, relevant results from authoritative sources (health organizations, medical clinics, evidence-based parenting resources). No paywalls or access issues were encountered.
